title: PgBouncer transaction mode
excerpt: Transaction pooling hands a server connection back after every COMMIT. Session state does not survive: SET, advisory locks, LISTEN and prepared statements all break or silently degrade. Client libraries differ in whether they warn. Use session mode if you need any of those.

title: Ingest worker architecture
excerpt: Workers pull from the Kafka topic, group records into batches and COPY them into the staging table, then a single upsert moves them into the partitioned target. Worker count is currently fixed at 32 and set in the Helm values.

title: Connection limits are an application concern
excerpt: Old note arguing the opposite of what I now think: that max_connections should be raised until the application stops erroring, and that pooling is a workaround for lazy client code. Written before I had seen a database fall over from context switching at 900 connections.

title: p99 latency on the write path
excerpt: Baseline measurements for the ingest write path taken in June: p50 8ms, p99 40ms at 4k rows/sec sustained. Measured at the worker, so it includes connection acquisition. Nightly batch window was excluded from this run.

title: COPY batch sizing experiments
excerpt: Rows per COPY versus WAL volume and transaction count, measured at 100 / 1k / 10k. Larger batches cut transaction count roughly linearly but raise the cost of a failed batch. No conclusion reached on the right number for production.

title: Prepared statements and the extended protocol
excerpt: What PREPARE actually does, when the planner reuses a generic plan, and why the fifth execution is where a custom plan gets replaced. Background reading; no project attached.

title: Weekly review 2026-W31
excerpt: Shipped the schema change. Interviewed two candidates. Bike had a puncture. Need to book the dentist and finish the migration doc before the freeze.

title: Kafka consumer group rebalancing
excerpt: Why adding a consumer stops the whole group briefly, the difference between eager and cooperative assignment, and the session timeout we settled on after the June incident.

title: Partitioned table upsert patterns
excerpt: ON CONFLICT against a partitioned table requires the conflict target to include the partition key, which our natural key does not. Three workarounds compared, including routing the upsert to the leaf partition from the application.

title: Helm values we always forget
excerpt: Replica counts, resource requests and the two annotations that control pod disruption budgets. Reference list, kept because these are never where anyone expects them.

title: Reading: tail latency is a distribution
excerpt: Notes on Gregg's argument that a single p99 number hides bimodal behaviour. The heat map is the point: two modes look identical to a percentile and completely different to a user.

title: Sourdough hydration log
excerpt: 80% hydration is too slack for this flour. 72% held shape through the second proof. Oven at 240C with steam for the first 15 minutes.
